title: LPST protest: Keralam CM Satheesan rules out lowering teacher-student ratio

ai.summary: Kerala's Chief Minister ruled out lowering the teacher-student ratio in government schools, stating it's already at 1:19 in many districts and would require adding teachers without financial means. The government agreed to four of five demands made by LPST rank-holders.

facts.claim: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan said lowering the teacher-student ratio from 1:30 to 1:25 is 'impractical'
facts.quote: Even as protests by the Lower Primary School Teacher (LPST) rank-holders are continuing in front of the Secretariat, Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Wednesday said that lowering the teacher-student ratio from the sanctioned 1:30 to 1:25 is “impractical” as the ratio is already down to 1:19 in government-run LP schools in the State.

facts.claim: The government agreed to four of five demands raised by LPST rank-holders
facts.quote: The government had already agreed to four of the five demands raised by the LPST rank-holders despite the additional financial burden involved.

facts.claim: In Malappuram, the ratio is down to 1:25, in Pathanamthitta and Kottayam 1:11, in Idukki 1:12 and Kannur 1:14
facts.quote: Government lower primary schools in Keralam has 3,49,000 students and 18,856 teachers at present. In Malappuram, the ratio is down to 1:25, in Pathanamthitta and Kottayam 1:11, in Idukki 1:12 and Kannur 1:14.

facts.claim: The Chief Minister blamed the Kerala Public Service Commission for conducting interviews and publishing rank-lists for non-existent vacancies
facts.quote: The Chief Minister also blamed the Kerala Public Service Commission for conducting interviews and publishing rank-lists for non-existent vacancies.

ai.background_note: Kerala government has agreed to four of five demands by LPST rank-holders, including extending rank-list validity and ensuring job security for appointments, but refuses to lower the teacher-student ratio which is already below 1:20 in many districts.
